name: US executive decision-maker
choices: Seek lawful economic or defense measures
limits: Congress, law, courts, agencies, and allies constrain action.
A playable person must hold the relevant office at the scenario date.

name: PRC senior decision-maker
limits: Party and military institutions affect implementation.
Do not infer perfect information or automatic compliance.

name: Taiwan executive decision-maker
limits: Legislative, legal, electoral, and commercial constraints apply.
Party victory alone gives no direct ownership of TSMC.

name: Taiwan legislator or party leader
choices: Propose, amend, or oppose a measure
limits: A single legislator cannot bind the legislature.
Different policy types have different legal procedures.

name: TSMC corporate decision-maker
limits: Boards, customers, workers, foreign inputs, and law constrain choices.
The firm cannot set Taiwan foreign policy.

name: Chip or equipment supplier
limits: Product qualification and licensing affect delivery.
A sale does not confer control of the buyer.

name: Export or AI regulator
limits: Authority is jurisdiction- and product-specific.
Regulators do not command foreign firms without a legal basis.

name: Allied government decision-maker
limits: Separate treaties and domestic authority apply.
A US request does not ensure approval.

name: AI developer or deployment operator
limits: A lab cannot issue state military orders.
Ownership, contracts, and regulator authority require separate checks.
A listed person controls only systems within their actual mandate.

name: Researcher or independent reviewer
limits: Advice is not command authority.
Access to evidence can be incomplete.
